remarks.name: Thibault Sottiaux
remarks.role: Codex & ChatGPT OpenAI
remarks.text:
On tokens and prices per token.

I said I’d write more about this, so here goes: an OpenAI token != another model’s token. We compare AI prices in dollars per million tokens as if a token were a standardized unit, like a gram or a kilowatt-hour. It isn’t. Different models use and produce the exact same text using different numbers of tokens, which means a lower price per token does not necessarily mean a lower bill.

Imagine two identical pizzas. One is cut into 8 slices at $2 each. The other is cut into 16 slices at $1.25 each. The second place advertises cheaper slices, but the whole pizza costs $20 instead of $16. Bummer ... your stomach doesn't actually care about the number of slices you just ate.

I know you are hungry now, but back to tokens. In one small comparison spanning English, technical, multilingual, and numerical text, the tokenizer we use for GPT-5.6 Sol used 766 tokens versus an estimated 1,170 for Claude Opus 5. That's a very significant difference of about 34.5% fewer tokens. You can get the same exact text, but pay for all those extra tokens. The price per token doesn't really tell this story.

Even correcting for tokenizer differences misses the bigger point. What actually matters is price per successful outcome, and for that you can use benchmarks as a starting point, but really you have to try it and measure on your own use cases.

That's all. May the tokens flow.
remarks.translation: 关于 token 和每个 token 的价格。我说过会多写一点，所以现在开始：OpenAI 的 token 不等于另一个模型的 token。我们习惯用“每百万 token 多少美元”来比较 AI 价格，好像 token 是一个标准化单位，就像克或千瓦时一样。但它不是。不同模型在处理和生成完全相同的文本时，使用的 token 数量并不相同，这意味着每个 token 的价格更低，并不一定代表最终账单更低。想象两个完全相同的披萨。一个切成 8 片，每片 $2。另一个切成 16 片，每片 $1.25。第二家宣传的每片价格更便宜，但整个披萨要 $20，而不是 $16。真扫兴……你的胃其实并不在乎你刚才吃了多少片。我知道你现在饿了，但回到 token。在一次涵盖英语、技术、多语言和数字文本的小范围比较中，我们用于 GPT-5.6 Sol 的分词器使用了 766 个 token，而 Claude Opus 5 估计使用了 1,170 个。这是一个非常显著的差异，大约少了 34.5% 的 token。你可以得到完全相同的文本，却要为所有那些额外的 token 付费。每个 token 的价格并不能真正说明这个问题。即使修正了分词器差异，也还是没抓住更关键的一点。真正重要的是每个成功结果的价格，而要做到这一点，你可以把基准测试当作起点，但最终必须在自己的使用场景中实际尝试和衡量。就这些。愿 token 流动不息。
remarks.observation: 这条言论适合观察模型运行、算力、存储、sandbox 或开发平台基础设施的变化；后续事实判断需回到原始公告或技术文档。

remarks.name: Guillermo Rauch
remarks.role: vercel CEO
remarks.text:
I think people don’t realize how much of the success of React is actually @shadcn.

I once referred to React as the actual “LEGO brick for adults.” But in reality it was more the description of the geometry of the bricks. The spec.

Shadcn is what people actually wanted from React. Reusable high quality components that also tunable. It’s a pseudo-library. There’s code but it’s actually meant to be digested into your context window and remixed.
remarks.translation: 我认为人们没有意识到React的成功有多少实际上归功于@shadcn。我曾把React称为真正的“成人版乐高积木”。但实际上，这更多是对积木几何形状的描述，即规格。Shadcn才是人们真正想从React中得到的东西。可重用且高质量、同时可调的组件。它是一个伪库。里面有代码，但实际上是旨在被消化进你的上下文窗口并重新混合的。
remarks.observation: 这条言论适合观察 AI 编程工具、设计到代码流程和软件生产方式的变化；需要结合产品发布或文档再做事实判断。

remarks.name: Swyx
remarks.role: achieve ambition with intentionality, intensity, integrity & insanity.
remarks.text: in case you’re not living in the tech bubble, as a general rule i’ve been surprised by how infrequently top tier folks actually meet/know each other. as an outsider i might have assumed that everyone is in secret illuminati group chats. those exist, but are very much short lived exceptions rather than the rule. what you see of the major headlines is pretty much what they also see. i guess one way to interpret this is also simply that most effort is still on doing the work rather than working the narrative or the gossip. and that, to me at least, is genuinely quite reassuring, this far in to my career.
remarks.translation: 如果你不是生活在科技圈里，一般来说，我一直很惊讶于顶尖人士之间真正见面或认识彼此的频率竟然如此之低。作为一个局外人，我可能会以为大家都在秘密的“光明会”群聊里。那样的群确实存在，但往往是短暂存在的例外，而非常态。你在重大新闻头条上看到的，基本上也就是他们看到的。我想，对此的一种解读也可以是：大多数精力仍然花在做事上，而不是经营叙事或八卦上。而这一点，至少对我来说，在职业生涯走到这么远之后，确实相当令人安心。

remarks.name: Peter Yang
remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
Tomorrow, I’m really excited to share a new episode with @rileybrown on how he uses Codex to run his entire content business.

I particularly loved watching him demo how he creates YouTube thumbnails with AI:

1. He uses Codex to find 100 top-performing thumbnails in his niche and add them to a Paper canvas.

2. He uses Paper to mix and match those thumbnails with photos of himself until he creates something he’s happy with.

Honestly, you have to watch the workflow to see how crazy it is.

📌 Subscribe to get the full episode tomorrow: https://t.co/NSTj7ijxE0
remarks.translation: 明天，我非常兴奋地要和大家分享一期新节目，邀请到@rileybrown，聊聊他如何利用Codex来运营整个内容业务。我特别喜欢看他演示如何用AI制作YouTube缩略图：1. 他用Codex在他的领域里找到100个表现最佳的缩略图，并把它们添加到Paper画布上。2. 他用Paper将这些缩略图与自己的照片混合搭配，直到做出满意的效果。说实话，你得亲眼看看这个工作流程，才能明白它有多神奇。📌 订阅以获取明天完整节目：https://t.co/NSTj7ijxE0

podcasts.originalTitle: Microsoft’s Vision for an Internet Made for Agents With CTO Kevin Scott (Best of the Pod)
podcasts.excerpt: 2025年，凯文·斯科特押注智能体网络将成为人工智能领域的下一件大事。这位微软首席技术官认为，要让智能体真正有用，它们需要能够代表我们采取行动——这意味着要让它们访问构成互联网的同样庞杂的工具、数据和系统。如今，这一赌注开始见效，因为智能体网络的基础设施正在建设中。在本周的AI & I节目中，丹·希珀重温了他与凯文的对话。他们讨论了微软在智能体网络中的角色、为什么开放性不必以牺牲安全性为代价，以及为什么程序员应该对新工具保持好奇，而不是出于原则而抵制它们。如果你觉得这期节目有趣，请点赞、订阅、评论并分享！想听更多丹·希珀的内容：订阅Every：https://…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: In 2025, Kevin Scott bet that the agentic web would be the next big thing in AI.The Microsoft CTO argued that for agents to be genuinely useful, they'd need to be able to take action on our behalf—which would mean giving them access to the same sprawl of tools, data, and systems that make up the internet. Today, that bet is starting to pay off, as the foundational infrastructure for the agentic web is now being built.On this week's AI & I, Dan Shipper revisits his conversation with Kevin. They discuss Microsoft's role in the agentic web, why openness doesn't have to come at the expense of security, and why programmers should stay curious about new tools rather than resist them on principle.If you found this episode interesting, please like, subscribe, comment, and share!To hear more from Dan Shipper:Subscribe to Every: https://…
